hypotheses.title: Object-type inclusion visibility check re-projects the whole included object once per member: O(M^2) per *T inclusion, O(N^3) on inclusion chains (stage 4)
hypotheses.issue: For every `*T` inclusion, collectIncludedMembers calls validateInclusionMemberVisibility, which loops over every member of the included type. For each member, inclusionMemberRegion calls semtypes.ObjectMemberVisibility(ctx, StringConst(name), T). That call converts the whole object to its mapping type (convertObjectToMappingTy) and runs full mapping-member projections (mappingMemberTypeInner -> bddMappingMemberTypeInner -> mappingAtomicMemberTypeInnerProj / mappingAtomicApplicableMemberTypesInnerProj -> getStringSubtypeListCoverage / stringListIntersect), each O(M) and allocating on every comparison. So validating one inclusion of an M-member type costs O(M^2) time and allocations, and a chain of N object types each including the previous one costs O(N^3). Every region recomputed this way is already stored in the included type's single object/mapping atom: one pass over the atom's fields, reading each member's small {value, kind, visibility} mapping, yields all M regions in O(M). At N=500, validateInclusionMemberVisibility accounted for 33% of CPU and 77% of all bytes allocated (2.1 of 2.8 GB), with GC taking about 44% of CPU.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a Ballerina program with a chain of N object types, each including the previous one
(type O<i> object { *O<i-1>; function m<i>() returns int; }), plus a class that implements the last
type so the program compiles and runs. Usage: gen_obj_inclusion_chain.py N > out.bal"""
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 500
out = ["import ballerina/io;", "", "type O0 object { function m0() returns int; };"]
for i in range(1, n):
    out.append("type O%d object { *O%d; function m%d() returns int; };" % (i, i - 1, i))
out.append("")
out.append("class C {")
out.append("    *O%d;" % (n - 1))
for i in range(n):
    out.append("    function m%d() returns int { return %d; }" % (i, i))
out.append("}")
out.append("")
out.append("public function main() {")
out.append("    O%d o = new C();" % (n - 1))
out.append("    io:println(o.m0() + o.m%d());" % (n - 1))
out.append("}")
print("\n".join(out))

improvement.summary: N=500 reproducer: wall time -58% (4.51 s -> 1.90 s, benchmark tool; hyperfine 4.41 s -> 1.74 s, 2.54x), peak memory -26% (585 MiB -> 431 MiB). N=750: 37.1 s -> 13.9 s (one run each, under load). A remaining superlinear cost is copying all inherited members into each including type's definition (inherent O(N^2) on chains).

hypotheses.fix_approach: Added semtypes.ObjectMemberVisibilities(ctx, ty) (map[string]string, bool). It takes ToObjectAtomicType once and, for each field of the atom, reads the 'visibility' field of that member's small 3-field mapping (CellInnerVal(atom.types[i])) with mappingMemberTypeInner + SingleShape, building a name->region map in O(M). validateInclusionMemberVisibility calls it once per inclusion and looks each member up in the map. When the type is not a single atom (e.g. records, or distinct/combined object types) it falls back to the old per-member ObjectMemberVisibility path. The rest-type member skip moved from inclusionMemberRegion into the loop so both paths skip it. Diagnostics are unchanged: for a single atom the old full lookup returned exactly that member's field type, and a non-field name gave a non-singleton 'string' region and was skipped, which is now a map miss. Pitfalls: distinct object types still take the slow path; a more general fix could memoize the region map per included type symbol, since the same type is often included many times. make test passed.

notes: Other candidates seen during exploration, not pursued: (1) the global pointer-keyed env.atomTable in semtypes/env.go:typeAtom never hits and holds ~500k entries, but removing it showed no consistent gain; (2) DiagnosticEnv.FileIndex RWMutex + map lookup per AST node location is about 1% of CPU.
